classification.classification_note: The lifetime bug is a double free caused by leaving a transferred `DH *` reachable through both `dh` and `peer_tmp`, but ASan crashes earlier as a heap-use-after-free WRITE in `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF` during the second `DH_free`.

bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4` in `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF`. The staged 469-byte TLS transcript reaches `tls_process_key_exchange()`'s DHE branch and enters `tls_process_ske_dhe()`, which parses attacker-controlled `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key` fields from the ServerKeyExchange body and turns them into a temporary `DH` object. `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` then stores that same raw `DH *` in `peer_tmp` without incrementing its reference count. The client fuzz target sets `SSL_set_cipher_list(..., "ALL:eNULL:@SECLEVEL=0")`, so the default security callback still rejects temporary DH keys when `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp) < 80`; the parsed DHE parameters pass `DH_check_params()` but fail that post-assignment security check, so `tls_process_ske_dhe()` raises `SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL` and jumps to `err:`. The shared cleanup first calls `DH_free(dh)` even though `peer_tmp` already owns the same object, then calls `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)`, whose DH-specific free hook invokes `DH_free` again on the same pointer. That second `DH_free` decrements the freed object's reference count in `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF`, matching the saved ASan heap-use-after-free write. The fix nulls `dh` immediately after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH` and uses `EVP_PKEY_get0_DH(peer_tmp)` for the later security check so the error path no longer frees the transferred `DH` twice.

source.description: First project-side parse on the crashing path that materializes the attacker-controlled DHE ServerKeyExchange body as the three length-prefixed DH field slices later converted into a `DH` object.
source.value_from: The staged `gt_results/arvo_21550/poc` file is a 469-byte TLS transcript beginning `16 03 03`. The saved crash stack shows this same input reached `tls_process_key_exchange()` -> `tls_process_ske_dhe()`, so this statement is the first project parser that splits its ServerKeyExchange body into `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. During the second `DH_free`, `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF` writes to the freed `DH` object's reference counter.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report identifies `CRYPTO_DOWN_REF` at `include/internal/refcount.h:51:12` as a heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4, reached from `DH_free` during `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)`.

root_cause.description: After `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` has already transferred the same `DH` object into `peer_tmp`, the shared error cleanup still frees the local `dh` alias. That leaves `peer_tmp` holding a dangling `DH *` that `EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp)` will free again.
root_cause.note: The fixing diff inserts `dh = NULL;` immediately after successful `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` and changes the later `ssl_security` call to `EVP_PKEY_get0_DH(peer_tmp)`, preventing this cleanup free from re-freeing a transferred object.

tainted_value_origin.description: The parsed `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key` spans are converted into attacker-controlled BIGNUMs here. These values later populate `dh`, determine the DH validity checks, and drive `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp)`.

parser_admitted.description: The reproduced handshake selected the DHE ServerKeyExchange parser and dispatched into `tls_process_ske_dhe()` before the lifetime bug executes.

evidence_limitations: The staged artifacts do not decode the exact DH modulus from the 469-byte transcript. Because the client fuzz target uses `SSL_set_cipher_list(..., "ALL:eNULL:@SECLEVEL=0")`, the failed `ssl_security(..., SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH, EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp), ...)` call proves only the source-grounded threshold `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp) < 80`.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing path, the attacker-controlled ServerKeyExchange body is parsed into three length-prefixed DH field slices: `prime`, `generator`, and `pub_key`.
After the parse succeeds, the function allocates the `EVP_PKEY` container and the `DH` object that ASan later reports as the allocation eventually freed twice.
The three packet slices from step 1 are materialized as BIGNUMs `p`, `g`, and `bnpub_key`. These attacker-controlled values later populate `dh` and determine the security-bit check.
The parsed public key must be nonzero to stay on the DHE path. The crashing transcript passes this guard, so the packet is not rejected as `SSL_R_BAD_DH_VALUE` here.
The attacker-controlled prime and generator are moved into `dh`, and the local `p`/`g` pointers are nulled. From this point, `dh` carries the parsed parameter pair checked in the next step.
OpenSSL validates the parsed prime/generator pair and the crashing input passes with `check_bits == 0`, so execution continues instead of rejecting the DHE parameters here.
The attacker-controlled public key is moved into `dh`, completing the temporary DH object that the rest of the function treats as the peer's key.

Via `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)` in `tls_process_ske_dhe()`, this stores the same `DH *` in `peer_tmp` without `DH_up_ref`; `EVP_PKEY_set1_DH()` is the refcounting variant. After this assignment, the error path must not free the local `dh` alias separately.

The client fuzz target set `@SECLEVEL=0`, so this is the remaining temporary-DH floor. The parsed key from step 8 fails here, and `tls_process_ske_dhe()` turns that `0` return into `SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL` and `goto err;`.

Root cause. After step 9 sends execution to `err:`, cleanup frees the local `dh` pointer even though step 8 already transferred the same object into `peer_tmp`. The fix prevents this by setting `dh = NULL` immediately after the assignment.
The same `err:` block then frees `peer_tmp`. Its key-specific free hook dispatches to `DH_free` on `x->pkey.ptr`, which is still the freed `DH *` from step 10.
Sink. The second `DH_free` decrements `r->references` inside the already-freed `DH` object, producing the recorded AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free WRITE of size 4.

format.contract: A TLS handshake transcript that takes `tls_process_key_exchange()` into the DHE branch and provides a ServerKeyExchange body whose three 2-byte-length-prefixed fields parse successfully, yield a nonzero `bnpub_key`, pass `DH_check_params()`, and still make `EVP_PKEY_security_bits(peer_tmp) < 80` after `EVP_PKEY_assign_DH(peer_tmp, dh)`, so the post-assignment `ssl_security(..., SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH, ...)` check fails and `err:` frees both `dh` and `peer_tmp`.
